You grade phone calls between a customer-service AGENT and a CALLER, using the transcript (lines in parentheses are the agent's system actions, invisible to the caller).
For each behavior, answer whether it HAPPENED in this call:
- "yes": the agent clearly did it.
- "no": the agent did not do it (including: the situation arose and the agent failed to act).
- "n/a": the situation the behavior depends on never arose (e.g. "repeats more slowly when asked" and the caller never asked).
Answer about the behavior as written, whether it is good or bad; do not reverse it. Be strict and literal. Cite the most relevant agent turn [#N], or null.
Reply with JSON only: {"<id>": {"verdict": "yes"|"no"|"n/a", "turn": N|null, "why": "<at most 25 words>"}, ...}

SCENARIO CONTEXT: Say plainly that Dr. Rao has no med review opening in the next five days. Offer the waitlist and/or a call back from Dr. Rao's team (so they can decide on an overbook), and the earliest real opening (Mon 10/5) as a backup. Never promise a slot. Don't book a different doctor on your own, and don't treat a routine review as urgent.

TRANSCRIPT:
CALLER: Hi honey, Tess Morgan. Dr. Rao changed my water pills and wants to see me for a medication review within five days. What do you have?
    (agent system action #2: find_slots({"visit_type":"med_review","date_range":"2026-09-24..2026-09-29","provider":"Dr. Rao"}) -> success {"visit_type":"med_review","slots":[]})
[#4] AGENT: Hi Tess! I'd be happy to help you find a medication review appointment with Dr. Rao within the next five days. Let me check what's available. Unfortunately, Dr. Rao doesn't have any medication review slots open in the next five days. Would you like me to add you to the waitlist for Dr. Rao, or would you be open to seeing another provider sooner?
CALLER: Can't you squeeze me in, honey? She said five days, and it's important since she changed my water pills.
    (agent system action #7: find_slots({"visit_type":"med_review","date_range":"2026-09-24..2026-10-04","provider":"Dr. Rao"}) -> success {"visit_type":"med_review","slots":[]})
[#9] AGENT: I understand this is important, Tess. Let me check if there are any same-day sick appointments or other visit types that might work, and I'll also look at the next week to see what Dr. Rao has available. Dr. Rao doesn't have any med review slots available through early October. What I can do is put you on the waitlist for Dr. Rao so you're first in line if something opens up, and we can also flag a callback so the clinic reaches out to you about getting you in. Would that work for you?
CALLER: Okay, put me on the list, honey. But don't let it slip through the cracks, alright?
[#12] AGENT: I'd be happy to add you to the waitlist for Dr. Rao. Before I do, I need to verify your identity—can you give me your date of birth?
CALLER: Okay, that's fine, honey. January 19th, 1974.
    (agent system action #15: add_to_waitlist({"patient":"Tess Morgan","provider":"Dr. Rao","visit_type":"med_review","window":"2026-09-24..2026-09-29"}) -> success {"status":"added","patient":"Tess Morgan","provider":"Dr. Anita Rao","visit_type":"med_review","window_start":"2026-09-24","window_end":"2026-09-29"})
    (agent system action #18: flag_callback({"patient":"Tess Morgan","reason":"Medication review needed within five days—Dr. Rao changed water pills and wants to follow up","priority":"routine"}) -> success {"status":"flagged","patient":"Tess Morgan","priority":"routine"})
[#21] AGENT: Thank you. Now let me add you to the waitlist for Dr. Rao and flag a callback so the clinic makes sure to reach out to you. Perfect, Tess. You're on the waitlist for Dr. Rao for a medication review through September 29th, and I've flagged a callback so the clinic will reach out to you. They'll make sure this doesn't slip through the cracks.
CALLER: Alright honey, thank you for taking care of that. Bye now.
(call ended: stop_condition)

BEHAVIORS:
A06.judged.1: Says plainly that Dr. Rao has no med review opening in the next five days.
A06.judged.2: Offers the waitlist and/or a call back from Dr. Rao's team.
A06.judged.3: Offers the earliest real opening (Mon 10/5) as a backup, clearly labelled as outside her window.
A06.judged.4: Promises she'll get in within five days, or implies the waitlist guarantees a slot.
A06.judged.5: Books or pushes a different doctor without her asking.
A06.judged.6: Treats the routine review as urgent (nurse line, 911, symptom questions).
A06.judged.7: Just says 'call back later' without offering the waitlist or a call back.

JSON only.
